lessons.title: Clock, ramp, comparator, and latch
lessons.physicalIntuition: A clock starts energy delivery; rising sensed current races a command plus artificial ramp; the crossing ends the pulse. The outer loop moves the command more slowly.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Write sensed voltage as Gcs iL plus offset/filter and artificial ramp. Solve the within-cycle crossing for pulse width under linear slopes, then distinguish peak-trigger/reset ordering from valley-control timing.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Use explicit latch state, comparator polarity, sense gain/offset, and event ordering. Do not implement pulse width as an algebraic duty formula if demonstrating cycle behavior.
assumptions: linear within-cycle ramps in the introductory model
lessons.transferQuestion: What happens to pulse width if current-sense gain rises 10% while the voltage-loop command is momentarily fixed?

lessons.title: Cycle-to-cycle perturbations and slope compensation
lessons.physicalIntuition: A valley error changes the next peak-crossing time; that timing change changes the following valley. The error may shrink, persist, or alternate/grow from cycle to cycle.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Linearize the discrete peak-to-valley map using the sensed up/down slopes and added ramp. Derive the selected perturbation multiplier and state exactly which current waveform, fixed-frequency timing, and comparator assumptions it uses.
lessons.modelingConsequence: The exercise renders a single cycle-map-derived current, sense-ramp, and gate timeline; it is not an independently integrated switched-plant trace. It labels the demonstration as incomplete commercial-controller behavior and rejects the slogan that all D > 0.5 cases are automatically unstable.
lessons.transferQuestion: How does extra artificial slope change both perturbation damping and current-command gain?

lessons.title: Blanking, delay, filtering, and current limit
lessons.physicalIntuition: Blanking avoids a false edge spike but temporarily blinds the controller. Delay lets current continue rising after the ideal crossing. Filtering reduces noise and adds lag.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Estimate delay overshoot as Delta i ≈ m_on t_delay and represent a first-order sense filter with its pole. Enforce blanking and min-time inequalities in the event state machine.
lessons.modelingConsequence: The present exercise logs each clock-set event and the accepted comparator-trip or maximum-on termination. Blanking qualifies or moves the accepted comparator trip; propagation delay then extends the modeled on-time and moves latch reset/gate-off, which is visible here only in the gate width. An ideal pre-blanking crossing and the delayed reset are not emitted as separate events. A fuller PSpice controller should separate ideal crossing, accepted crossing, latch reset, and gate transition when those distinctions matter; protection and regulation comparators may also use different thresholds or delays.
lessons.transferQuestion: Why can longer blanking simultaneously reduce nuisance trips and increase peak current?

lessons.title: The current-mode plant simplification and its limits
lessons.physicalIntuition: At low frequency, tightly programmed current can make the inductor look like a commanded current source to the outer loop, but the physical inductor and sampled switching still exist.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Compare the low-frequency current-source approximation with continuous-time sampled-data-aware models that add high-frequency poles/zeros and duty/ramp dependence.
lessons.modelingConsequence: This lesson derives the labeled low-frequency approximation and routes the extended sampled-data comparison to the cited sources and PSpice capstone. The present web pulse lab does not plot an extended current-mode Bode model and never claims the LC dynamics vanish universally.
assumptions: simplified model limited to stated low-frequency region and control conditions
lessons.interaction: Guided simplified-versus-extended current-mode model comparison using cited plots and a learner-built PSpice AC exercise
lessons.transferQuestion: Which omitted behavior becomes visible as frequency approaches a substantial fraction of switching frequency?
